prose.title: The Lycian Revolt
prose.summary: The six Lycian cities of Patara, Xanthos, Tlos, Limyra, Myra and Telmessos break away from whoever holds them, at the campaign start the Ptolemaic Empire, and form the Lycian League. It can come early when one of the cities rebels under Rhodian or foreign rule, and otherwise happens at the end of the Seleucid Empire's turn in turn 102 (245 BC).
prose.breaks_away_from: The Ptolemaic Empire, or whoever holds the Lycian cities at the time
prose.who_it_can_happen_to: Any campaign, whoever holds the Lycian cities, human or AI.
what_sets_it_off: If one of the six Lycian cities rebels, and Rhodes has held 3 or more of the six at the end of more than 10 Seleucid turns in total (not necessarily in a row), the whole of Lycia revolts.

From turn 72 (253 BC), if one of the six cities rebels while 4 or more of the six were held, at the end of the last Seleucid turn, by factions other than the Ptolemaic Empire, the Seleucid Empire and Rhodes (rebels included), the whole of Lycia revolts.
If it has not yet happened and the Seleucid Empire still exists, the revolt fires at the end of the Seleucid Empire's turn in turn 102 (245 BC), whoever holds the cities.
From turn 152 (233 BC), if the Seleucid Empire is gone and the revolt has still not happened, any one of the six cities rebelling sets it off.
what_happens: Patara, Xanthos, Tlos, Limyra, Myra and Telmessos all rebel against whoever holds them.
All six cities pass to the Lycian League, which did not exist until now.
Each city gets a garrison at 0.01 times normal strength, drawn from Akontistai, Greek Slingers, Lycian Archers, Lycian Marines, Lycian Hoplites, Lycian Drepanophoroi, Prodromoi and Xystophoroi.
When Patara revolts, the Lycian League receives 10000 denarii.
The revolt happens only once per campaign.
prose.playing_as_the_rebels: If you, the human player, held at least one of the six Lycian cities at the last check before the revolt (made at the end of each Seleucid turn), a message titled 'The Lycian League declares its independence!' appears at the end of the next Seleucid turn and offers to let you play as the Lycian League. If you accept, you switch to playing the Lycian League and a government building is placed in Patara, Xanthos, Tlos, Limyra, Myra and Telmessos. No offer is made if you held none of the six cities, or if the Seleucid Empire has no further turn.
